headline: Triangles are the strongest shape—they can't deform without breaking, which is why bridges and towers use them
universal_truth: Strength comes from structure, not just material; how things are arranged matters as much as what they're made of
fun_facts: Push on a rectangle and it collapses into a parallelogram—push on a triangle and it holds firm
The Eiffel Tower uses 18,000 iron pieces mostly arranged in triangles for structural strength
Ancient Egyptians built pyramids with triangular faces—the shape has survived millennia
discussion_questions: Why can't triangles deform the way rectangles can?
Where do you see triangles used for strength in everyday structures?
What 'triangles' provide stability in your life—things that can't easily collapse?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Press on a square and it squishes into a diamond. Press on a triangle and it doesn't budge. Triangles are the only polygon that can't deform without breaking—which is why every bridge, tower, and crane uses triangular bracing. The shape is the secret to strength.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Rectangles seem stable—buildings are usually rectangular. But engineers reinforce everything with triangles. What makes triangles inherently stronger than other shapes?

options.text: Triangles distribute force along their sides, and their fixed angles mean they can't deform without sides breaking
options.response: Yes. A triangle's angles are fixed by its side lengths—change one and you break it. Rectangles' angles can shift while sides stay intact. Triangles resist distortion.

options.text: Triangles have fewer sides, so there's less that can break
options.response: Fewer sides isn't the reason—it's about how forces distribute and angles lock...

q1.title: Rigid Geometry
q1.script: Here's the secret: a triangle's angles are determined by its side lengths. You can't change the angles without changing the sides. Rectangles can shift into parallelograms—same sides, different angles. Triangles can't. They're geometrically rigid.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Rigid Geometry"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Force Distribution
q2.script: When weight presses on a triangle, the force travels down both sides and spreads to the base. The shape distributes load efficiently. That's why roof trusses, bicycle frames, and bridge structures are triangulated—triangles share the burden.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Ancient Wisdom
q3.script: Pyramids are the oldest monumental structures still standing. Their triangular faces distribute weight outward and downward. The Egyptians discovered what engineers still use: triangular forms resist time and gravity.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Strength comes from structure, not just material. Triangles teach that how things are arranged matters as much as what they're made of. The same materials, differently organized, yield different strength.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 173. Tomorrow, we'll explore shapes that tile perfectly—tessellation. Until then, look for triangles in structures around you—bridges, cranes, buildings. They're hiding in plain sight.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Structural Thinking - Arrange for Strength
growTrack.learning_objective: Apply triangular thinking to life stability
growTrack.activity: Identify 'triangles' in your life—stable structures with three connected elements. Work-health-relationships? Learning-practice-feedback? What arrangements give your life rigidity against pressure? Structure creates strength.
